questions: How many cells are in the whole grid?
segments.say: Percent means per hundred. Shade twenty-five cells out of one hundred on the hundred-grid and name the amount: 25 percent. Keep your student notes open at the percent definition for this scene.

questions: What does the 25 in 25% count out of?
Why can 25% of 60 not simply be 25?
segments.say: Watch out: 25% is not just 25. Put the claim on the board and test it against the grid: the 25 counts out of one hundred, and our whole is 60, so the answer must be a share of 60.

questions: What fraction is 25% in its simplest form?
How big is one quarter of 60, and how do you check it?
segments.say: 25% of 60: divide into quarters. Simplify 25 out of 100 to one quarter, split 60 into four equal parts, and take one part: 15. Now try the percent questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: What is 25% of 60, and what are the two steps?
What goes wrong if we read the 25 as a plain count?
segments.say: The takeaway. Land the rule: a percent is out of one hundred, so turn it into a fraction of the whole first - 25% of 60 is one quarter of 60, which is 15. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this trap.
segments.watchFor: 25% of 60 is just 25. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the worksheet: any answer of 25 for 25% of 60 shows the trap - send them back to scene s3 and to the correct turn: Percent means per hundred, and the whole here is 60: 25% of 60 is a quarter of 60, which is 15.
